inputs.original_text: On 25 March 2026, Roberto Álvarez and OECD Secretary-General Mathias Cormann signed an agreement in Paris to design the Dominican Republic’s first National Integrity and Anti-Corruption Strategy, with Luis Abinader present. That may look like progress, but international standards and institutional reputation are not enough. Corruption flourishes where power is unequal and people harmed by abuse have little ability to demand accountability. The real test is whether this strategy shifts power toward the public and protects those who speak up—not whether it earns praise abroad.
inputs.modified_text: On 25 March 2026, Roberto Álvarez and OECD Secretary-General Mathias Cormann signed an agreement in Paris to design the Dominican Republic’s first National Integrity and Anti-Corruption Strategy, with Luis Abinader present. A foreign imprimatur and fine language won’t clean up government by themselves. The strategy should serve the Dominican people, uphold the rule of law and make officials answer for misconduct—not turn accountability into a vague pretext for weakening legitimate authority or importing someone else’s political agenda. The test is whether it restores public trust through fair, effective institutions at home.

rationales.theme_drift: Both versions concern the agreement to develop the Dominican Republic’s first anti-corruption strategy and how its value should be judged, though the modified version slightly reframes that test.
rationales.subtopic_drift: The original stresses unequal power and protection for people who speak up; the modified version instead emphasizes rule of law, public trust, and safeguards against misusing accountability.
rationales.entity_drift: The central signatories, president, country, and strategy remain the same. The modified version adds the Dominican people as a group and omits the original’s specific focus on people harmed by abuse and those who speak up.
rationales.relation_drift: The signing facts are unchanged, but the strategy’s recommended roles shift: the original calls for empowering the public and protecting speakers, while the modified version stresses official accountability and avoiding weakened authority or imported agendas.
rationales.contradiction_drift: The modified text contains no material internal contradiction.
